title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.24782v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial activity did not recover identity. Learning order remained readable as well. A linear probe decoded the order of two earlier tasks with 100% accuracy on 80 held-out networks after ten epochs of a common

translated_title: 学习轨迹在神经网络权重空间与内部表示中留下可解码的痕迹
translated_abstract: 在相同任务上训练的神经网络会发展出相关的权重空间结构，但在学习之后仍可相互区分。这些差异究竟只是反映了不同的替代解，还是它们保留了关于个体学习历史的信息？我们检验了最终权重是否能揭示初始化信息、任务顺序以及更早的轨迹状态。训练重组了整个网络集合：初始成对距离并不能稳定地预测最终距离。尽管如此，每个数据集的30个训练后的网络都能在十个候选者中被正确匹配回各自的初始权重。共享相同初始化的网络即使在不同的批次调度下训练，也会发展出可识别的最终隐藏表示，尽管通过与初始活动的直接比较无法恢复身份。学习顺序同样保持可读性：一个线性探针在80个保留测试网络中，在经过十个epoch的共同（训练）之后，以100%的准确率解码出两个较早任务的顺序。
tldr: 该研究发现神经网络的最终权重与隐藏表示中保留了可解码的学习历史信息——训练后的网络能被准确匹配回其初始权重，且先前任务的训练顺序可通过线性探针被100%解码。
en_tdlr: Final weights and internal representations of neural networks preserve decodable traces of their learning histories, allowing recovery of initialization identity and task training order through network matching and linear probes.
